ROOT P2 PREPARATION: CRITICAL RAYLEIGH PROJECTION, AMPLITUDE TRANSFER, NONLINEAR LIMIT
10 November 2026 Brisbane. Mathematical source/representation work; no new scientist post, no full common-force theorem and no novelty claim for imported literature.

EXPLICIT CRITICAL SPLITTING. In angular square-torus variables, fix horizontal Fourier p=+1 or-1 and no third-direction frequency l=0. Put Q=-d_y^2+1, H=I-Q^-1, P the y-constant projection. Then HP=0, H commutes with P,Q, and on (I-P)L2 the Fourier eigenvalues H_m=m^2/(m^2+1) lie in[1/2,1]. The critical Rayleigh vorticity equation for a real integrable amplitude a(t) is
 w_t=-nu*Qw-i*p*a(t)*sin(y)*H w.
Writing b=Pw,v=(I-P)w gives EXACTLY
 v_t=-nu*Qv-i*p*a(t)*(I-P)sin(y)*H v,
 b_t=-nu*b-i*p*a(t)*P sin(y)*H v.
The first equation is closed; the kernel does not force its complement. The reverse coupling is generally present, so an arbitrary kernel projection of the full solution must not simply be declared autonomous free heat.

DIRECT ENERGY AND PAID NORM BOUND. Since H is positive on the complement, z=H^(1/2)v satisfies a diffusion plus bounded skew-adjoint perturbation whose selfadjoint factor is H^(1/2)(I-P)sin(y)H^(1/2). Consequently
 d/dt ||H^(1/2)v||2^2=-2nu*<Q H v,v>,
 ||v(t)||2<=sqrt(2)||v(0)||2,
 |b(t)|<=e^(-nu*t)|b(0)|+sqrt(2)*integral_0^t|a(s)|ds*||v(0)||2.
Thus the complete critical Rayleigh group has a polynomial-in-amplitude-action bound C*(1+integral|a|), not an a priori exp(integral|a|) necessity. This statement concerns this linear vorticity fibre. It does NOT make the anomalous kernel contract rapidly: if v(0)=0, b(t)=e^(-nu*t)b(0) exactly. It also does not prove terminal echo cancellation of the inhomogeneous kernel term. A733's k_i=0 echo is a DIFFERENT sector.

KNOWN COMPLEMENT OPERATION, GOVERNING SOURCE READ. Lin-Xu, https://arxiv.org/pdf/1707.00278v1, Eq1.3, Theorem1.1(ii), Section2.2 Eq2.11-2.12 and Lemma2.7. ROOT read the square-torus projection, positivity, continuous-spectrum argument and RAGE interface. The theorem controls the non-anomalous component for the decaying background e^(-nu*t), uniformly over its L2 initial vorticity as viscosity tends tozero. Its nonlinear square-torus result has a small-vorticity condition and an infimum-time conclusion; it is not unrestricted fixed-endpoint control.
